ca_north_face_lower.blurb: The lower tier of the big wall on Crafts Peak in the San Bernardino Mountains, sitting at roughly 7,900 feet. There are nine trad routes, running from 5.7 up to the low 5.11 range, with the bulk of them between 5.9 and 5.10. Expect mostly crack lines, plus a few face climbs that carry some lichen. The wall is the lower half of a two-level cliff, so it pairs naturally with the upper tier above.

ca_oasis_rock.blurb: A large formation in Joshua Tree National Park, set directly behind Rat Rock in the Barker Dam area. It holds nine trad routes, ranging from 5.7 to 5.11, with most falling in the 5.10 band. The lines include a dihedral, some face climbing and one technical 5.11 test piece. Getting to the base means skirting Rat Rock and a bit of scrambling and boulder hopping. Because the Barker Dam area spreads its routes over several separate formations, you can combine a visit here with neighbouring rocks.

ca_octagon_north_face_the.blurb: A boulder in Blair Valley, in the desert of San Diego County, at about 2,700 feet. This is the steep, shaded side of the Octagon and holds nine problems. There is one easy V1 warm-up, then a run of hard lines: mostly V5 to V9, including several V6s and a couple of V9 traverses and sit starts. Holds are on the sharp side. It is the harder face of the Octagon, so beginners will find little here beyond the warm-up wall.

ca_cuckoo_s_nest.blurb: A small crag near the top of Donner Summit in the I-80 corridor of the Lake Tahoe area, at about 7,000 feet, with a view out over Donner Lake. It holds nine routes, five sport and four trad, with a few top-rope options. Grades run from 5.9 to 5.12, centred on 5.11. There are three ways in, each taking around half an hour but varying in steepness. Donner Summit is snowed in through winter, so plan for summer, spring or fall.

ca_one_eyed_cat_wall.blurb: An east-facing wall at the south end of Voodoo Garden, in the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles near Big Bear Lake in the San Bernardino Mountains, at around 7,500 feet. There are nine routes: six sport and three trad, including one long trad line. Most of the sport lines are 5.10, with a few easier trad routes from 5.6 to 5.8. The climbing is on thin edges and good plates. The wall can be seen from the road, so it is easy to spot, and the walk in is short.

ca_overhang_pinnacle.blurb: A blocky pinnacle in the Shooting Gallery, part of the Lake Arrowhead Pinnacles in the San Bernardino Mountains, at about 4,900 feet. It has nine routes, five sport and four trad, mostly from 5.5 to 5.9 with one 5.11 sport line. Several of the routes here are among the longer ones in the Shooting Gallery. That mix of easy bolted lines and short trad climbs makes it a reasonable stop for newer leaders, and the approach shares the walk used for the rest of the sector.

ca_owl_rock.blurb: A small tower in the Lower Kern River Canyon in the southern Sierra, at around 2,000 feet and east of Bakersfield. Climbing here is all trad: nine routes up cracks and chimneys, from an easy fifth-class line to 5.9, most of them 5.9 and 5.8, with two carrying aid ratings. The approach is an uphill trek, so long pants and boots are a good idea.
